tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome, Commander!
tutorial.welcome1: I am PUSULA, your helper robot. Together we keep the base running for 30 sols. A sol is one day on Mars.
tutorial.welcome2: Follow the bouncing arrow. Tap a station and Ada walks there.
tutorial.s1.clean: The landing left dust on the solar panels. Tap the solar panels and clean them: clean panels make more power.
tutorial.s1.moxie: Now the air. Tap the oxygen machine and make oxygen. It uses some power.
tutorial.s1.end: Well done! Every job takes daylight hours. Go to the habitat and end the day.
tutorial.s2.moxie: Each night the base uses air and power. Make oxygen again and watch both gauges: air goes up, power goes down.
tutorial.s2.clean: Dust is back on the panels. Clean them so the Sun can fill the power again.
tutorial.s2.end: Power comes back while the Sun shines. Keep enough for the night heating, then end the day at the habitat.
tutorial.s3.greenhouse: The greenhouse is open! Tap it and tend the plants to grow food.
tutorial.s3.clean: Dust is back on the panels. Clean them to keep the power up.
tutorial.s3.end: You know the basics now. End the day at the habitat. Tomorrow more places open.
unlock.title: New today
unlock.greenhouse: Greenhouse: tend the plants to grow food.
unlock.food: New gauge, Food: the crew eats one portion every night.
unlock.shelter: Shelter: pile up Mars soil to make it stronger, and wait inside during a particle storm.
unlock.antenna: Antenna: repair it to message Earth and to hear storm warnings earlier.
unlock.beacon: Landing marker: later it shows the rescue ship where to land.
unlock.curiosity: Curiosity spot: read the rover's real radiation measurement to earn science.
unlock.science: Science spot: scan a rock to earn science.
unlock.dose: New gauge, Storm dose: it fills when a particle storm from the Sun reaches Mars. Keep it low.

pusula.sunNews: Sun news for {date}: {n} solar flare alert(s) near Earth. No direct effect on our base.
tip.sol: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
tip.moxie: MOXIE is a real machine: on the Perseverance rover it made oxygen from Mars air for the first time in 2021.
tip.dust: Dust is a real problem: the InSight lander stopped working in 2022 when dust covered its solar panels.
tip.delay: A radio message between Mars and Earth takes from about 4 to 24 minutes, depending on where the planets are.
tip.field: Mars has very thin air and no magnetic shield around the whole planet, so particles from the Sun can reach the ground.
tip.rad: The Curiosity rover has measured radiation on Mars with its RAD instrument since 2012.
tip.quietSun: When the Sun is quiet, more cosmic rays arrive: Curiosity measured about 9 µGy per hour in 2019 and about 5 in May 2024.
tip.lettuce: NASA study OSD-268 is about lettuce grown on the International Space Station.
source.rad: Source: NASA OSDR RadLab, Curiosity RAD
source.game: Game event (made up, not real data)
info.power.title: Power
info.power.uses: Night heating, the oxygen machine, the greenhouse and messages to Earth use it.
info.power.how: The solar panels make power while the Sun shines. Clean panels make more.
info.power.fact: Dust really settles on solar panels on Mars: the InSight lander ran out of power in 2022 because of it.
info.air.title: Air
info.air.what: Oxygen for the crew to breathe.
info.air.uses: Breathing uses it every sol. A cold night without heating uses even more.
info.air.how: Make oxygen at the oxygen machine. It needs power.
info.air.fact: Mars air is mostly carbon dioxide. The real MOXIE machine on the Perseverance rover turned it into oxygen.
info.food.title: Food
info.food.uses: The crew eats one portion every night.
info.food.how: Tend the plants in the greenhouse. Do not leave them alone for too long.
info.food.fact: NASA study OSD-268 is about lettuce grown on the International Space Station.
info.dose.title: Storm dose
info.dose.what: The share of the mission's storm dose budget that is used. Only particle storms count: everyday cosmic rays are not counted. This is a game scale.
info.dose.uses: Particle storms from the Sun fill it. The real curve measured by Curiosity decides how fast.
info.dose.how: Make the shelter stronger before a storm and wait inside while it lasts. The gauge never goes down.
info.dose.fact: Curiosity's RAD instrument measures radiation on Mars. In this month its quiet level was {rate} µGy per hour. In the game 1 point is {uGy} µGy of storm dose.
info.science.title: Science
info.science.what: Stars for what the crew learns on Mars.
info.science.uses: Nothing uses it up. More science gives a better mission result.
info.science.how: Read Curiosity's measurement and scan a rock, once per sol each.
info.science.fact: The Curiosity rover has explored Gale Crater on Mars since 2012.
event.dust.fact: Dust storms are real on Mars: in 2018 one covered the whole planet. This storm is made up for the game.
event.sep.mars: Real data: on {date} Curiosity's RAD instrument measured this storm on Mars. The early warning is a game simplification.
event.sep.earth: This solar particle storm really happened on {date}. It was measured near Earth; its effect on Mars is simplified for the game.
event.reply.fact: A radio message between Mars and Earth takes from about 4 to 24 minutes, depending on where the planets are.
event.report.title: Yesterday's storm
event.report.mars: On Mars: Curiosity's RAD measured up to {n} µGy per hour that day. The quiet level is {quiet}.
event.report.earth: Near Earth: DONKI lists {n} particle storm report(s) for that day.
event.report.earthNone: Near Earth: DONKI lists no particle storm for that day. A storm does not reach every planet the same way.
night.why.calm: A calm night: heating and breathing are the normal costs of every sol.
night.why.cold: Why so much air? Power ran out, so the heating stopped. Keep more power for the night.
night.why.foodEmpty: The food store is empty. Tend the plants tomorrow.
night.why.dust: The dust storm dimmed the Sun, so the panels made less power and got dirty faster.
night.why.broken: A broken station is still waiting for a repair.
night.why.radEvent: The storm dose changed because a particle storm reached Mars today.
whatif.title: What if?
whatif.sheltered: Good call: you took {got}% because you waited in the shelter. With no shelter time it would be {alt}%.
whatif.missed: If you had waited {h} hours in the shelter, today's storm dose would be {alt}%. You took {got}%.
